title: Sabalenka's US Open Prep Hits Another Snag as 20-Year-Old Bejlek Stuns World No. 1 in Cincinnati
summary:
Aryna Sabalenka's rocky road to the US Open took another unexpected turn on Thursday as she squandered commanding leads in a 7-6 (9-7), 6-4 loss to 20-year-old Sara Bejlek in the fourth round of the Cincinnati Open. The Belarusian top seed led 5-1 in the first-set tiebreak and 4-1 in the second set, but the Czech qualifier rallied both times to claim the biggest win of her career.

The defeat is a significant blow for Sabalenka, who is aiming to become the first woman since Serena Williams in 2014 to win three consecutive US Open titles. The New York major begins on August 30, but Sabalenka's preparation has been far from ideal: she suffered early exits in both Cincinnati and Toronto, and since winning the 'Sunshine Double' at Indian Wells and Miami in March, she has reached just one semifinal. Her position as world number one is now precarious — Elena Rybakina could overtake her if she reaches the Cincinnati final.

For Bejlek, ranked 35th, it was a landmark victory. 'I totally lost my words,' she said. 'I just keep believing and that was the key today. She played amazing tennis and I was just believing, keep fighting and I was just trying my best and that's it.' It was her first win over a top-10 opponent and her first WTA 1000 quarterfinal. She will face former Australian Open champion Madison Keys next.

Meanwhile, in the men's draw, Tommy Paul staged a dramatic comeback against Alexander Zverev, winning 4-6, 7-6 (8-6), 6-4 after saving a match point. Paul will play Flavio Cobolli in the quarterfinals.
why_it_matters: This upset shows how fragile a top athlete's form and ranking can be, even after a dominant spring; for young players like Bejlek, it demonstrates that belief and composure can topple the established elite.

background_read: The Cincinnati Open (a WTA and ATP 1000 hard-court tournament held in Mason, Ohio) is traditionally one of the final major tune-up events before the US Open, so a top player's early exit there can signal trouble.

Aryna Sabalenka (the Belarusian world No. 1 known for her powerful serve and groundstrokes) entered the match trying to become the first woman since American legend Serena Williams in 2014 to win three straight US Open titles.
Sabalenka won the 'Sunshine Double' at Indian Wells and Miami in March — two of the most prestigious 1000-level tournaments outside the Grand Slams — but has struggled since then.

Sara Bejlek (a 20-year-old Czech qualifier ranked 35th at the time) had never beaten a top-10 player before, making the upset part of a broader WTA pattern in which lower-ranked young players can challenge the very top.
The ranking context is crucial: Elena Rybakina could overtake Sabalenka for world No. 1 by reaching the Cincinnati final, showing how quickly the top of the women's game can shift.

perspectives.description: For Bejlek, this is a landmark career achievement and validation of her fighting spirit. Her win shows that a qualifier can stay composed against the world No. 1 and turn huge deficits into victory.
Blowing a 5-1 tiebreak lead and a 4-1 second-set lead raises concerns about Sabalenka's closing ability and mental toughness. With the US Open near, her early exits suggest preparation is off track.

The result reflects the current depth of women's tennis, where a qualifier ranked outside the top 30 can beat the top seed. It also shows how ranking points create a precarious battle for No. 1 between Sabalenka and Rybakina.

Bejlek now faces former Australian Open champion Madison Keys, a match that will reveal whether her run is a turning point. For Sabalenka, the question is whether she can fix her serving and closing before the New York major.
